schoolPressures.detail: His elder son missed what would have been his first PUC year because he was needed for cotton-picking.

schoolPressures.label: Costly commutes
schoolPressures.detail: The nearest PUC with a science stream needs a daily bus commute the family judged too costly.

schoolPressures.label: Bad monsoon
schoolPressures.detail: A poor monsoon can turn into hired labour or short migration for the whole family.

schoolPressures.label: Girls' care work
schoolPressures.detail: His daughter helps with cooking and sibling care after school, which can make girls fall behind.

pressures: His elder son missed his first PUC year for cotton-picking. When the crop needs hands, schooling is what gets traded away, and his younger children face the same choice.
The PUC with a science stream needs a daily bus commute the family judged too costly, so the fee and fare decide the stream, or whether the next child continues.
A poor monsoon can turn the whole family to hired labour or short migration, taking children out of class for the season.
Falling behind is what makes leaving feel reasonable later, so his daughter's after-school chores are an early step toward her exit.
factorEffects.sanitation: If his household lacks a proper toilet, his daughter, who already juggles cooking and sibling care, would be the first to miss school.
factorEffects.district: The factor flags the share of English-medium schools in Kalaburagi. The card shows cotton season, commute cost and a bad monsoon as what costs his children school, not language.

changes.effect: A stocked school library would give his children a place to study; at home, cotton-season work and care work leave little time for it.
Repaired classrooms would keep lessons running for his sons and daughter, especially in a bad monsoon, one of the pressures on his family.
Kalaburagi ranks last in Karnataka for continuous evaluation, so a child who misses weeks in cotton season may only be found to be behind at the SSLC exam.

lag.factor: % Population Living in Households with Improved Sanitation
lag.effect: Kalaburagi also has the lowest household-sanitation share in the state; if his home lacked a toilet, his daughter would face the risks that keep older girls at home.

schoolPressures.label: Secondary costs
schoolPressures.detail: Transport, uniforms and notebooks outweighed her son's potential wage once school was outside the tanda.

schoolPressures.label: Daily wages
schoolPressures.detail: Even small daily wages can outweigh a classroom seat when the household is short of cash.

schoolPressures.label: Monsoon roads
schoolPressures.detail: Poor road connectivity to some tandas makes attendance harder in the monsoon months.

schoolPressures.label: Language gap
schoolPressures.detail: Gor Boli at home, Kannada at school; her younger daughter needed an extra year to adjust.

pressures: Transport, uniforms and notebooks outweighed her son's potential wage once school was outside the tanda, so the cost of continuing is what decides it for him.
Her husband is a daily-wage labourer, so any wage a child can earn looks large next to a classroom seat in a lean week.
Poor roads into some tandas make attendance hardest in monsoon months, so a child can fall behind for weeks at a time.
At home the family speaks Gor Boli but school is in Kannada. Her younger daughter needed an extra year to adjust, which is a quiet way to fall behind.
factorEffects.sanitation: If her tanda household lacks a proper toilet, her two daughters' attendance would suffer first, adding to cost and distance.
factorEffects.district: The factor flags the share of English-medium schools in Ballari. The card's own language gap is Gor Boli at home to Kannada at school, and costs and wages are what she names as pressures.

changes.effect: Ballari's schools have nearly full toilet coverage but still rank among the lowest in the state; a working girls' toilet is what lets her two daughters stay through the day.
Safe, repaired classrooms would keep her children's lessons going in the monsoon, when bad roads already make the trip to school hard.
Regular checks would show early if her children are slipping, perhaps because of the language gap they face, before the SSLC exam decides it.

lag.effect: Ballari has among the fewest teachers per student in Karnataka; in large classes, a child who struggles with the school's language gets little help.
